updates.label: Energy market update
updates.headline: XLE climbs 2.6% as Brent settles near $116.72.
updates.summary: Energy led Friday's session. Brent crude futures settled at $116.72, up about 3.1% on the day, and the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) closed at $69.33. Watchlist energy names followed, with Matador Resources up about 5.6%, the United States Oil Fund up about 4.3%, and ConocoPhillips up about 3.6%.

about.summary: XLE is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the energy companies in the S&P 500, mainly oil and gas producers, refiners, and equipment and services firms.
uses: Tracks the large-cap US energy sector in one fund
Often moves with crude oil and natural gas prices
Used as a reference point for energy sector sentiment
about.note: This is news, not financial advice.

updates.label: Tech market update
updates.headline: QQQ and XLK steady after Thursday's tech drop.
updates.summary: Large-cap tech held its ground Friday after a sharp Thursday decline. QQQ closed at $704.40, nearly flat, after falling about 2.9% on Thursday. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) added about 0.5% to $183.23. Meta Platforms extended its slide, closing at $642.62 after a roughly 7% drop on Thursday.

about.summary: QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq. XLK tracks the technology companies in the S&P 500.
uses: QQQ is a common gauge of large-cap growth and tech stocks
XLK offers focused exposure to the S&P 500 tech sector
Both are used to follow software, semiconductor, and SI-related names
about.note: This is news, not financial advice.

updates.label: Broad market update
updates.headline: SPY slips 0.5% as the Dow ETF falls about 1.2%.
updates.summary: Broad US stocks ended the week lower. SPY closed at $759.97, down about 0.5%, its second straight decline. The SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) fell about 1.2% to $521.37, while higher oil prices lifted energy shares.

about.summary: SPY is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500, a benchmark of 500 large US companies across all sectors.
uses: Widely used as a gauge of the overall US stock market
Serves as a benchmark for sector and single-stock performance
Holds every S&P 500 sector, including tech and energy
about.note: This is news, not financial advice.

updates.label: Crypto market update
updates.headline: HYPE reaches a new all-time high near $91.79.
updates.summary: HYPE moved into price discovery after clearing its prior record near $89.61. The move followed new borrowing utility on Hyperliquid and Payward's plan to build regulated U.S. perpetual markets through Hyperliquid HIP-3.

about.summary: HYPE is the native token of Hyperliquid, a layer-one blockchain built for onchain financial markets. Hyperliquid has two connected parts: HyperCore for spot and perpetual-futures order books, and HyperEVM for smart-contract applications.

uses.label: Network security
uses.value: HYPE can be delegated to validators through HyperCore's proof-of-stake system.

uses.label: Transaction fees
uses.value: HYPE pays gas fees when users and applications make transactions on HyperEVM.

uses.label: Market infrastructure
uses.value: Some HyperCore actions, including native-token deployment, require fees paid in HYPE.

about.note: HYPE is a volatile crypto asset. It is not a dollar-pegged stablecoin.

catalysts: Hyperliquid launched manual borrowing. Users can supply HYPE or BTC as collateral and borrow USDC or USDT.
Payward, Kraken's parent company, intends to deploy U.S. perpetual futures markets through Hyperliquid HIP-3. The plan remains subject to regulatory approval.
updates.risk: HYPE is extended and has no established resistance above the new high. At 9:14 AM ET, Robinhood showed a $89.85 bid and $91.61 ask. That wide spread increases execution risk. Borrowing against HYPE can also add liquidation pressure during a sharp decline.
updates.disclaimer: Research and education only. This is not a buy or sell recommendation. Crypto trades continuously, and prices can change quickly.
